title: TDLR — Privacy Exposure
description: The redundancy is concentrated in exactly the data you least want duplicated.

data_source.query: FROM tdlr-forms | STATS `Forms requesting SSN` = COUNT(*) WHERE MV_CONTAINS(sensitive_pii_fields, "ssn")

FROM tdlr-forms | STATS `Identity-theft trifecta` = COUNT(*) WHERE MV_CONTAINS(sensitive_pii_fields, "ssn") AND MV_CONTAINS(sensitive_pii_fields, "dob") AND MV_CONTAINS(sensitive_pii_fields, "driver_license_number")
FROM tdlr-forms | STATS `Forms requesting criminal history` = COUNT(*) WHERE MV_CONTAINS(sensitive_pii_fields, "criminal_history")
FROM tdlr-forms | MV_EXPAND reuse_tier_state_of_record | STATS `State-of-record field entries` = COUNT()
FROM tdlr-forms | MV_EXPAND field_category_instances | STATS instances = COUNT() BY field_category_instances

config.title: Forms requesting data TDLR already holds

data_source.query: FROM tdlr-forms | MV_EXPAND reuse_tier_state_of_record | STATS form_count = COUNT_DISTINCT(form_id) BY reuse_tier_state_of_record | SORT form_count DESC

config.title: How many ways TDLR spells each canonical field

data_source.query: FROM tdlr-forms | MV_EXPAND field_alias_pairs | DISSECT field_alias_pairs "%{canonical} :: %{raw}" | STATS variant_count = COUNT_DISTINCT(raw), forms = COUNT_DISTINCT(form_id) BY canonical | SORT variant_count DESC
